title: The names wheat hides behind
standfirst: Wheat goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name wheat when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to wheat is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to wheat is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 28 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA), Pub. L. 108-282, Title II — wheat named as a major food allergen
FASTER Act of 2021, Pub. L. 117-11 — confirms the Big-9 major allergens (wheat retained)

Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex II point 1 — 'Cereals containing gluten, namely: wheat (such as spelt and khorasan wheat), rye, barley, oats or their hybridised strains'; plus Annex II exemptions for wheat-based glucose syrups incl. dextrose, wheat-based maltodextrins, glucose syrups based on barley, and cereals used for distillates
21 CFR Part 137 — Cereal Flours and Related Products (standards of identity for wheat flour, bromated flour, self-rising/enriched flour, durum, semolina, farina)
21 CFR 101.91 — 'Gluten-Free' Labeling of Foods Final Rule (defines wheat, barley, rye, crossbred hybrids as gluten-containing grains)
Wheat Allergy — allergen fact sheet and hidden-source list (semolina, durum, farina, kamut, spelt, seitan, HVP, surimi)

sources.authority: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies
sources.doc: Scientific Opinion on the evaluation of allergenic foods and food ingredients for labelling purposes (EFSA Journal 2014;12(11):3894) — cereals containing gluten
CXS 118-1979 (rev. 2015) — Standard for Foods for Special Dietary Use for Persons Intolerant to Gluten; defines gluten-source grains

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not wheat. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
